clusters.notes:
WHAT THE AUDIT GOT RIGHT: all four claims are factually accurate. Every file:line checks out.

WHAT IT GOT WRONG / OVERSTATED:

1. Severity is not uniform across the four sub-claims, and lumping them under one P0 hides that. Only two are real automated gates: the missing SystemBootTime category (P0-01c) and the missing appex manifests (P0-01d). The CA92.1-vs-1C8F.1 issue (P0-01b) is NOT an upload blocker — Apple's automated validator checks that the category has a reason string from the approved set for that category, and CA92.1 is a valid UserDefaults reason. Calling it a submission blocker would misallocate release-day panic. Fix it anyway (one word), but do not gate on it.

2. The audit missed VaultifyAutoFillMac entirely. It names "VaultifyAutoFill / VaultifySafari" but Project.swift:260-312 defines a third appex with the same `sources: ["VaultifyAutoFill/**", "VaultifyCore/**"]` glob, the same missing manifest, and it ships in the Mac App Store slice. Three appexes, not two.

3. The audit did not check the biggest actual privacy defect here: GoogleAppMeasurement 12.16.0 ships as a STATIC archive (`file` says "current ar archive") with NO PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy anywhere in the xcframework — verified against its own code-signed resource list. A static lib cannot carry a manifest into the app bundle, so its collection lands on the app's manifest, and `strings` on that archive shows `identifierForVendor` x4. The app collects a Device ID and declares none. That is worse than a wrong reason code for a password manager.

VERIFIED NON-ISSUES (do not "fix" these, they will just add false declarations):
- Vaultify/Services/Artifacts/ArtifactStore.swift:161 `FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath:)[.size]` — FileAttributeKey.size is NSFileSize, which is on neither the file-timestamp nor the disk-space list. `attributesOfItem` itself is not a listed API. No FileTimestamp category needed.
- Vaultify/Services/Developer/ProvisioningProfileInspector.swift:21/44 `creationDate` — a local struct field and a `dict["CreationDate"]` plist read from an embedded mobileprovision. Not a filesystem API.
- Vaultify/Services/Sharing/ApprovalSpike.swift:155,163 `latest.creationDate` — CKRecord's CloudKit property. Semantically not a required-reason API. Low-confidence caveat only: it compiles to the bare Obj-C selector `creationDate`, which is the same string Apple's file-timestamp list names, so a symbol-level scan could in principle false-positive. If an ITMS-91053 email ever cites FileTimestamp with no matching source, this is where to look first. Not worth pre-emptively declaring.
- Zero disk-space APIs (volumeAvailableCapacity*/statfs/statvfs/NSFileSystemFreeSize) and zero active-keyboard APIs (activeInputModes) anywhere in Vaultify/, VaultifyCore/, VaultifyAutoFill/, VaultifySafari/, VaultifyAutoFillMac/.
- GoogleUtilities' FileTimestamp (C617.1) and UserDefaults (1C8F.1/C56D.1) usage is covered by its own manifests — it is a SOURCE SPM target, so SPM emits GoogleUtilities_Privacy.bundle into the app. Same for FirebaseCore, Crashlytics, GoogleDataTransport, nanopb, promises. Do not duplicate those into the app manifest.

CONFIRMING THE QUESTION YOU ASKED ABOUT APPEX COLLECTION: yes, declaring analytics/crash collection in the APP manifest is correct and the appex manifests must declare an EMPTY NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes. Project.swift gives the appex targets no `.package(...)` dependencies (only the app target links FirebaseAnalyticsCore and FirebaseCrashlytics at lines 149/155), so the appexes collect nothing. Copying the app manifest into them would be a false declaration and would pollute the aggregated Xcode privacy report.

EXECUTABLE-BY-EXECUTABLE REQUIRED-REASON MAP (the thing the audit should have produced):
- Vaultify.app (iOS + macOS): UserDefaults CA92.1 + 1C8F.1 (VaultifyCore/SharedConfig.swift:27, ThemeReader.swift:12+35, plus ~60 .standard sites) AND SystemBootTime 35F9.1 (Haptics.swift:62). Plus statically-linked GoogleAppMeasurement's `initWithSuiteName` — covered by CA92.1 (its own private suite).
- VaultifyAutoFill.appex: UserDefaults CA92.1 + 1C8F.1 only (VaultifyCore + CredentialProviderViewController.swift:27,279). No boot time.
- VaultifyAutoFillMac.appex: identical to VaultifyAutoFill.
- VaultifySafari.appex: UserDefaults CA92.1 + 1C8F.1 only (VaultifyCore's WebExtensionRouter.swift:89, WebExtensionSaveGate.swift:30-121). No boot time.

One shared ExtensionResources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy therefore serves all three appexes. Keep it out of VaultifyCore/, VaultifyAutoFill/ and VaultifySafari/ so the `sources` globs cannot pick it up, and remember `tuist generate` is required before it exists in any target.

UNRESOLVED: I could not empirically confirm whether Apple's ITMS-91053 scan resolves an appex binary's usage against the host app's root manifest or demands a per-bundle manifest. Apple's docs do not state it unambiguously. The fix is two lines per target, so this is not worth resolving before shipping — just add them.

clusters.notes:
Blunt assessment.

WHAT THE AUDIT GOT RIGHT: P0-02's URL claim is fully confirmed and is a genuine submission blocker, for a sharper reason than "the URLs are wrong". The paywall is NOT dark in review. LooxEntitlementStore.swift:145-167 grants beta purchase access on `appStoreReceiptURL.lastPathComponent == "sandboxReceipt"` alone, before it even tries AppTransaction — TestFlight and App Review both hit that branch, so purchasesEnabled is true and the reviewer sees LooxAcquisitionPaywallView with two 404 links. LooxMembership's own comment says the pages "must resolve before purchasesEnabled ever flips" while the lines above document that beta flips it anyway; the invariant was written and contradicted in the same file.

WHAT IT MISSED (same area, all verified):
1. AboutView.swift:175 ships "Loox collects no analytics and has no accounts" in EN/VI/JA while PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares three collected data types and both toggles default true. That fact is worse than the 404 and nobody flagged it. AboutView.swift:159-160 "Nothing is sent to a server" is false too. The marketing site has an automated claims-honesty gate (frontend scripts/claims-gate.sh); the app, where users actually read the claim, has none.
2. LooxPaywallScreen.swift:113 presents a second purchase surface (SubscriptionStoreView) with zero policy links — `subscriptionStorePolicy*` appears nowhere in the repo. Fixing the LooxMembership constants alone does not close 3.1.2.
3. termsURL/privacyURL appear on exactly ONE screen. A user who never opens the paywall has no in-app path to the privacy policy at all — newly relevant now that the app does collect data.
4. The breach-check toggle is documented three different ways (macOS says it talks to Google, iOS Security says nothing, Watchtower has the correct k-anonymity text).

WHAT I'D PUSH BACK ON: if the audit framed default-on analytics as an App Review blocker, that is overstated. PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is filed correctly, FirebaseAnalyticsCore carries no IDFA, NSPrivacyTracking is false, so no ATT prompt is owed and Apple does not require a consent gate for non-tracking analytics. It is a GDPR/ePrivacy exposure and a trust problem, not a rejection — the rejection risk comes from the About-page contradiction and the App Privacy questionnaire answers, not from the default itself. Also, opt-out-by-default is a documented deliberate design (SettingsStore.swift:106-125), so flipping the default is an owner decision, not something to change under an audit finding.

On question 6 specifically, plainly: `FirebaseApp.configure()` is gated ONLY on the presence of GoogleService-Info.plist (FirebaseAnalyticsProvider.swift:15-23). Consent is applied afterwards via `Analytics.setAnalyticsCollectionEnabled` (AnalyticsEngine.swift:49 → provider :37-39). Firebase persists that flag itself, so an opted-out user stays dark on later launches — but on launch #1 of a fresh install the default is true, the SDK initialises, and events (including OnboardingFlow.swift:115 tutorialBegin) leave the device before the user has seen a single word about it. There is no first-run disclosure anywhere in the app. Crashlytics collection is disabled only in DEBUG (CrashReporter.swift:65-73), so TestFlight and App Review builds do upload reviewer crashes.

Not probed per instruction, still open: whether s.looxpassword.com, invite.looxpassword.com (AASA), config.looxpassword.com/v1/*, entitlement.looxpassword.com and the support@looxpassword.com mailbox are actually live in production — TestFlight is a Release build and uses the production constants, not the staging ones.

findings.evidence: Store default is genuinely off: /Users/bervion/Developer/Projects/mobile/ios/Vaultify/Vaultify/App/SettingsStore.swift:234 `iCloudSyncEnabled = d.bool(forKey: Key.icloud)` (UserDefaults.bool -> false when unset; contrast the neighbouring opt-out flags at :231-:239 which use `d.object(...) as? Bool ?? true`). Onboarding overrides it: OnboardingFlow.swift:143 `env.settings.iCloudSyncEnabled = true`, inside `createVault(_:)` (lines 135-155), unconditional, executed for EVERY newly created vault immediately after `try await env.session.createVault(...)`. Two distinct pushes follow, both before the user has seen the word iCloud: (1) OnboardingFlow.swift:149 `addFolder(...)` -> VaultRepository+Folders.swift:70 `noteLocalMutation()` -> VaultRepository.swift:137 posts `.vaultLocalMutation` -> SyncCoordinator.swift:41-44 -> `scheduleDebouncedSync()` (:76-84, guard passes because the flag is now true) -> a real CloudKit write ~3s later, while the user is still typing their name on NameStepView; (2) OnboardingFlow.swift:103-109 `.task(id: step)` -> `recoveryKey = (try? await env.session.generateRecoveryKit()) ?? ""` then `env.syncNow()` -> SyncCoordinator.runSync() (:86-110) -> `cloudSync.sync(...)` -> CloudSyncService.swift:113 `modifyRecordZones(saving: [zone])` + :154-178 push of all 8 planes + :117 pull, then :97 `escrow.pushRecoveryEnvelopeIfNeeded()` and :107-108 `pushService.ensureSubscribedIfNeeded()` + `deviceRegistry.publish()`. Exactly what leaves the device at that moment: ItemRecord -> `sealed` ciphertext + PLAINTEXT `createdAt/updatedAt/metaUpdatedAt/favorite/pinned/archived/isDefaultIdentity/trashedAt/deletedAt` (CloudSyncService.swift:347-365; `useCount`/`lastUsedAt` deliberately withheld, :361-363); FolderRecord -> `sealed` + PLAINTEXT `iconAsset`, `colorRaw`, `sortIndex`, timestamps (CloudSyncService.swift:387-398); VaultKeyEnvelope -> `wrappedByRecovery` (the Vault Key wrapped under the recovery-key KEK), `recoverySalt`, `kdf` JSON (VaultKeyEscrowService.swift:78-90); VaultDevice -> PLAINTEXT `UIDevice.current.name`, marketing model name, app version (DeviceRegistryService.swift:83-92, :174-186). Onboarding copy, read end to end, mentions iCloud ZERO times in the create path: WelcomeLandingView.swift:189 actually says the opposite ("keys stay only on this device"), CreateMasterPasswordView.swift:12-13/:87, NameStepView.swift:33-35, EmergencyKitView.swift:40-42/:226, ChooseThemeView.swift:22-24, EnableBiometricView.swift:20-22, OnboardingFlow.swift:190-194 recap. The ONLY disclosure is inside the saved PDF (EmergencyKitPDFPage.swift:111 "Anyone who has this kit and access to your iCloud can restore your vault"), which the user reads after the envelope has already uploaded.
findings.realRisk: A privacy-first, "zero-backend" password manager silently starts a CloudKit zone in the user's private database during first run. Concretely a user sees: Settings > iCloud Sync already ON without ever touching it; a CKSubscription registered; their device name and model in a CloudKit record; and, if not signed into iCloud, a permanent error status row ("Sign in to iCloud to sync.", CloudSyncService.swift:124) for a feature they never asked for. Not an App Review rejection (a user's own private CloudKit DB is not "data collected by the developer" under Apple's nutrition-label rules), but it directly contradicts the shipped README and any privacy-first positioning, and it is the exact class of thing a security-minded reviewer or a competitor screenshots. NOTE for whoever fixes this: deleting line 143 is NOT a safe fix on its own — `pushRecoveryEnvelopeIfNeeded()` is reached only through the `guard settings.iCloudSyncEnabled` at SyncCoordinator.swift:90, so with sync off the Emergency Kit PDF's own instruction (EmergencyKitPDFPage.swift:127 "install Loox, sign in to the same iCloud, then scan the Setup Code") becomes a lie and JoinByRecoveryView dead-ends on `Failure.noEnvelope`. The fix is a consent decision, not a deletion.

The write sites that turn approval mode ON (SettingsScreen.swift:69, ShareAccessSheet.swift:348, ShareSpaceSheet.swift:282, VaultShellBehaviors.swift:189, ApprovalSpike.swift:69/:199, LooxHubScreen.swift:408) never touch iCloudSyncEnabled, and the sync toggle (SyncSettingsView.swift:15-26) never touches approvalModeEnabled. The ADR is also documented in-code at SettingsStore.swift:92-95, SettingsScreen.swift:60-62, ApprovalCoordinator.swift:39-40, ApprovalSpike.swift:24, OwnerShareRefresher.swift:15, SharedZoneSubscriptionService.swift:9/:20.

findings.claim: generateRecoveryKit() is wrapped in try?, swallowing errors.
findings.evidence: OnboardingFlow.swift:104-109: `if step == .emergencyKit, recoveryKey.isEmpty { recoveryKey = (try? await env.session.generateRecoveryKit()) ?? "" ; if !recoveryKey.isEmpty { env.syncNow() } }`. The audit understated this — the consequence is a hard, unescapable dead-end, not a swallowed log line. On failure `recoveryKey == ""`, and then: EmergencyKitView.swift:205-207 renders `ProgressView()` forever in place of the key; EmergencyKitView.swift:82-84 `BrandCapsuleCTA(title: "Save Kit PDF", enabled: !recoveryKey.isEmpty, ...)` is permanently disabled, and the Continue variant at :77 is unreachable because it requires `savedPDF`, which only the fileExporter success at :93-95 can set. There is no back control on this step (OnboardingFlow.swift:54-55, "No back: the identity seeds ran when the name step completed") and no retry: `.task(id: step)` only re-fires when `step` changes, and step is pinned at `.emergencyKit`. The user's only exit is force-quitting; on relaunch `onboardingCompleted` is still false (RootView.swift:22) so the flow restarts at .welcome, and re-running create calls VaultSession.swift:128-146 `createVault`, which unconditionally `try bundle.save()` with a BRAND NEW vault key — the folder and identity seeded in the first attempt become undecryptable and land in `quarantined` (VaultRepository.swift:69-82). Contrast the correct handling of the identical call in RegenerateKitView.swift:171-183, which catches and shows "Couldn't generate a new recovery key. Please try again." clusters.notes:
Blunt assessment of the audit report on this cluster.

WRONG — item 6 (ADR-2 cross-gating). There is no coupling. I read all 35 call sites of the two flags. Sharing gates on approvalModeEnabled only; sync gates on iCloudSyncEnabled only; the only joint writes are the two deliberate teardowns (AppEnvironment.swift:131-132 DEBUG isolation, :409-410 eraseEverything), both setting BOTH to false, which is correct. Do not spend effort here. The only real gap is that nothing tests it (NEW-3).

WRONG IN DETAIL — item 4's data inventory. The audit says folder records carry "PLAINTEXT fields like FolderRecord.iconAsset and name". The NAME is not plaintext: FolderRecord.swift:11-12 keeps it inside `sealed` (AES-256-GCM under the Vault Key), and CloudSyncService.swift:390 uploads `sealed`, not a name. Plaintext folder fields are exactly iconAsset, colorRaw, sortIndex, and timestamps. Overstating this weakens an otherwise correct finding — the honest version is still bad enough, and the app's own Settings footer (SyncSettingsView.swift:39) already discloses precisely this set, which shows the team knows the real boundary.

MISSED — the audit inventory also omits DeviceRegistryService.publish() (DeviceRegistryService.swift:83-92), which uploads `UIDevice.current.name`, the marketing model name and the app version in plaintext on the same first sync. That is the most identifying plaintext in the whole payload.

UNDERSTATED — item 7's `try?` on generateRecoveryKit. The audit framed it as a swallowed error. It is an unescapable onboarding dead-end: empty key -> permanent ProgressView + permanently disabled CTA, no back control on that step, and `.task(id: step)` cannot re-fire because step never changes. The only exit is force-quit, and re-running create overwrites the vault key so the seeded data is orphaned into `quarantined`. Probability is low; severity if hit is total.

OVERSTATED — item 7's enableBiometric claim. The state does NOT go inconsistent: VaultSession.swift:239-253 throws before setting `biometricUnlockEnabled`, and the done-step recap reads that flag, so the copy stays truthful on failure. And advancing anyway is a documented deliberate decision (VaultSession.swift:240-245) — per the repo's own review rules, that is a verified prior decision and should not be reversed on an abstract concern. Only the missing user feedback is a real (minor) defect.

OVERSTATED — item 7's "Add your first item" copy. An identity IS seeded (OnboardingFlow.swift:51/:169), so the sentence is imprecise, but it is a polish nit, not a P0. Its VI and JA translations are present and correct.

CORRECT AND WORSE THAN STATED — the core P0-03 claim. Two things sharpen it: (a) the first upload fires on a 3-second debounce during the NAME step, not at the Emergency Kit step, so a fix scoped to `env.syncNow()` alone would not close it (NEW-2); (b) the comment justifying the line is factually false about being a "no-op" (NEW-1), which is plausibly why it survived review.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES P0-03: do not just delete OnboardingFlow.swift:143. `pushRecoveryEnvelopeIfNeeded()` is reachable only through the `guard settings.iCloudSyncEnabled` at SyncCoordinator.swift:90, so with sync off, the Emergency Kit PDF's printed restore instructions (EmergencyKitPDFPage.swift:127) become false and JoinByRecoveryView dead-ends on `.noEnvelope`. This needs a product decision about what the Emergency Kit means without iCloud, not a one-line deletion. That decision belongs to the user, not to the audit — present the trade-off rather than silently picking a default.

App Review reality check: this will not get the build rejected. Data in the user's own CloudKit private database is not "collected by the developer" under Apple's nutrition-label rules, and I found no App Store description in the repo (no fastlane/metadata/) making a contradictory claim. I marked P0-03 blocksSubmission=true anyway, on the product/trust argument — README.md:117-118 and the welcome screen's own "keys stay only on this device" (WelcomeLandingView.swift:189) are shipped statements the binary contradicts. If the team disagrees with that judgement, the fix is still cheap (M) and the doc fix (S) is non-negotiable either way.

findings.claim: Website-icon lookups are ON by default and send the full host of every stored login to Google (www.google.com/s2/favicons), contradicting the product's "offline / zero-backend / never leaves the device" positioning and the shipped privacy manifest.
findings.evidence:
Vaultify/App/SettingsStore.swift:237 — `showWebsiteIcons = d.object(forKey: Key.favicons) as? Bool ?? true` (default ON; contrast SettingsStore.swift:234-236 where iCloudSyncEnabled/approvalModeEnabled/artifactSyncEnabled use plain `d.bool(...)` = default OFF).
Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:42 — `URL(string: "https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?sz=128&domain=\(host)")`. The host is the un-truncated, un-hashed registrable+subdomain host (FaviconService.swift:21-27 only lowercases and strips a leading `www.`). No k-anonymity, unlike the HIBP path.
FaviconService.swift:46 — `try? await URLSession.shared.data(from: url)`. No custom URLSessionConfiguration anywhere in Vaultify/ or VaultifyCore/ (grep for URLSessionConfiguration/URLCache/ephemeral returns zero hits), so this uses the default disk URLCache and the shared HTTPCookieStorage.
Render-triggered, not save-triggered: FaviconView.swift:47 `.task(id: faviconLoadKey)` with faviconLoadKey = urlString (FaviconView.swift:51). Every row that mounts fires one request. Call sites confirmed: Vaultify/Features/Vault/VaultItemRow.swift:24 (used by HomeScreen.swift:952, ArchiveScreen.swift:19, TrashScreen.swift:24, MacItemListColumn.swift:23, VaultItemRowLink.swift:24), Vaultify/Features/Home/HomeSection.swift:76, Vaultify/Features/Home/Components/AttentionCell.swift:53, Vaultify/Features/Home/Components/TotpCardView.swift:35, Vaultify/Features/ItemDetail/ItemDetailScreen.swift:508, Vaultify/Features/ItemEditor/ItemEditorScreen.swift:515, Vaultify/Features/ItemEditor/WebsiteFieldRow.swift:47, Vaultify/Features/Passkeys/PasskeysScreen.swift:81, Vaultify/Features/Passkeys/PasskeyDetailSheet.swift:17, Vaultify/Features/ImportExport/ImportView.swift:67. Search results AND shared-item results go through VaultItemRowLink (SearchScreen.swift:348/368/373/398) and SharedWithMeScreen.swift:25.
No rate limiting or batching exists — FaviconService.swift is 53 lines total; the only throttle is the `inFlight` set (line 12).
Declaration gap: Vaultify/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy:22-60 declares exactly three types (ProductInteraction, CrashData, OtherDiagnosticData) and NSPrivacyTrackingDomains is an empty array (line 20-21). Nothing covers disclosing the user's site list to Google. README.md:3-6 states "never leaves the device — no account, no server. The only telemetry is anonymous usage statistics (GA4...)" — false while this is default-ON.
WHAT IS CORRECT AND THE AUDIT MAY HAVE UNDERSOLD: there IS an explicit, honest, fully localized in-app disclosure. GeneralSettingsView.swift:86-88 footer: "Uses Google to fetch site icons as login avatars. This reveals the sites you have logins for to Google; turn off to keep everything on-device." Same text at MacSettingsView.swift:133-135. Vaultify/Localizable.xcstrings has vi + ja translations for both that string and "Show website icons".
findings.realRisk: Google (and any on-path observer, since the domain is in a plaintext query string even under TLS via SNI/timing correlation) receives the full host of every login the user views. Timeline: nothing on save; a burst on first render of Home/Vault/Search after unlock, one request per visible row, then one per row as the user scrolls; the whole set is enumerated within a few minutes of normal use. Because URLSession.shared uses the shared cookie jar, Google's NID cookie ties all of those hosts to one persistent pseudonymous identity across launches. Searching is worse: as matching rows appear, Google learns which of the user's sites matched — including SHARED items (SearchScreen.swift:373). Concretely: a user with a login for a psychiatric clinic, a specific bank, and an adult site has all three hosts at Google within a minute of opening the app, having agreed to nothing. For Apple: the ASC App Privacy answers must cover a third-party disclosure of browsing-history-adjacent data; the repo-side manifest shows no one has thought about that. The default-ON choice itself is a legitimate product decision (1Password/Bitwarden do the same but against their OWN icon servers, not Google) — do not silently flip it, but the README claim and the privacy declaration cannot both stand as written.
changeScope: Vaultify/App/SettingsStore.swift:237 — decide explicitly: keep `?? true` (product decision) or change to `d.bool(forKey: Key.favicons)` for default-OFF. If it stays ON, the remaining items below are mandatory.

Vaultify/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy — add an NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes entry covering the disclosure (NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeBrowsingHistory or NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeOtherDataTypes, Linked=false, Tracking=false, purpose AppFunctionality), and update the file's leading comment which currently asserts collection is "two things and nothing else".
README.md:3-6 — drop or qualify "never leaves the device" and "The only telemetry is anonymous usage statistics"; name the default-ON favicon egress.

Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:42 — if the domain leak is unacceptable at all, replace the Google endpoint with a direct `https://<host>/favicon.ico` fetch (leaks the domain only to the site the user already has an account with) or a self-hosted icon proxy on the existing Loox control-plane host.
Vaultify/Features/Onboarding/ — surface the choice once at onboarding rather than burying it in Settings → General (optional, but it is what turns a disclosure into consent).

findings.claim: The favicon cache lives in the App Group container, is named by plaintext domain, is written with no file protection, and is never cleared — not by Erase Vault, not by remote sign-out, not by toggling the setting off.
findings.evidence:
FaviconService.swift:16 — `cacheDir = cacheDirectory ?? SharedConfig.containerURL.appending(path: "Favicons")`. SharedConfig.swift:113-124 resolves that to the shared App Group container (group.com.bervion.vaultify) — the same directory as Vault.store, so it is inside the backed-up container, not Caches/ and not tmp/.
Filename scheme: FaviconService.swift:32 and :50 — `cacheDir.appending(path: "\(host).img")`. The DIRECTORY LISTING alone is a plaintext enumeration of every site the user has a login for. No hashing, no sealing — the bytes are the raw PNG from Google.
File protection: FaviconService.swift:50 — `try? data.write(to: ...)` with NO options. Compare VaultifyCore/Keychain/VaultKeyBundle.swift:55 (`options: [.atomic, .completeFileProtection]`) and VaultifyCore/Sharing/SharedCredentialsCache.swift:90-91 (same). FaviconService.swift:17 also creates the directory with no `attributes:`. So the domain list sits at the OS default class (CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication) — readable while the device is locked-but-booted, a strictly weaker class than every other file this app writes to that container.
Erase: Vaultify/App/AppEnvironment.swift:384-416 `eraseLocalState()` clears sharingStore, looxLinks.records, sharedItems, notificationHistory, quickViewHistory, SharedCredentialsCache, SharedItemsProjection, AuditLocalCache, VaultKeyEscrowService fingerprint, ParticipantEscrowService, RelayPrincipalEscrowService, SharedZoneSubscriptionService, DeviceRegistryMirror, flips approvalModeEnabled/iCloudSyncEnabled off, repository.clear(), artifactStore.eraseAll(), store.eraseAll(), uiState.wipe(), session.resetVault(). `faviconService` appears nowhere in that function — the whole file references it only at AppEnvironment.swift:19 and :210. FaviconService itself exposes no clear/purge/wipe API (the file is 53 lines; there is none).
Toggle-off: FaviconView.swift:61 reads `env.settings.showWebsiteIcons` inside `load()`, which only runs from `.task(id: faviconLoadKey)` (line 47) keyed on urlString (line 51). So flipping the toggle off correctly stops FUTURE fetches (any newly-mounted row bails at line 61-62) but does not re-run load() on already-mounted rows — previously fetched icons keep rendering until the view is rebuilt — and purges nothing.
findings.realRisk: "Erase Vault" is the feature a user reaches for when they are handing the phone over, selling it, or believe they are compromised. After it completes, `<AppGroup>/Favicons/` still contains one file per site — chase.com.img, protonmail.com.img, grindr.com.img — at a protection class that survives a locked device, and it is inside the iTunes/Finder-backup set (unlike Caches/). The same list survives a remote "Log Out Device" wipe (handleRemoteSignOut → eraseLocalState). The vault ciphertext is gone; the metadata that actually identifies the person is not. The erase function's own doc comment enumerates residue file-by-file, so this is an omission, not a design choice.
changeScope: Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift — add `func clearCache()` that removes `cacheDir` and empties `memory` and `inFlight`; change line 50 to `try? data.write(to: ..., options: [.atomic, .completeFileProtection])`; pass `attributes: [.protectionKey: FileProtectionType.complete]` (iOS-only, #if os(iOS)) to the createDirectory at line 17; store under a hashed filename (e.g. SHA256(host) hex + ".img") so the directory listing stops being a site inventory.
Vaultify/App/AppEnvironment.swift:384-416 — call `faviconService.clearCache()` inside `eraseLocalState()`, next to the other cache wipes at lines 395-408.

Vaultify/App/SettingsStore.swift:105 — either drive a purge from the didSet, or (cleaner, since SettingsStore must not depend on a service) purge in the Settings toggle handler in Vaultify/Features/Settings/GeneralSettingsView.swift:82 and Vaultify/Features/Settings/MacSettingsView.swift:127 when the value goes true→false.

Vaultify/Features/Components/FaviconView.swift:51 — fold the setting into faviconLoadKey (e.g. `isAuto && env.settings.showWebsiteIcons ? urlString : nil`) so toggling off also drops already-rendered icons in the same session.
tests: FaviconServiceTests.testClearCacheRemovesDiskAndMemory — seed a cache dir via the injectable `cacheDirectory` init param, call clearCache(), assert the directory is empty and a subsequent cachedIcon(host:) returns nil
FaviconServiceTests.testCacheFilenameDoesNotContainHost — write a favicon for "example.com" and assert no file in cacheDir has "example" in its name

findings.claim: When two items share the same host, only ONE row gets its icon on first load; the others silently fall back to the category badge for the rest of the session.
findings.evidence: FaviconService.swift:41-44 — `guard !inFlight.contains(host), let url = ... else { return nil }` / `inFlight.insert(host)` / `defer { inFlight.remove(host) }`. The in-flight guard RETURNS NIL to the second caller instead of awaiting the first result. FaviconView.swift:64 — `image = await env.faviconService.fetchIcon(host: host)`, so that nil becomes the row's final state, and FaviconView.swift:47 `.task(id: faviconLoadKey)` will not re-run because the id (urlString, line 51) has not changed.
findings.realRisk: Two Gmail accounts, or a work + personal login on the same site — extremely common in a password manager — render inconsistently: the first row shows the favicon, the second shows the tinted category badge. It self-heals only if the row is recycled by a lazy stack (scroll off and back). On a short Home list with no scrolling it stays wrong until the screen is rebuilt. Purely cosmetic, but it looks like a rendering bug in the first screen the user sees.
changeScope: Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:11-12,39-52 — replace the `inFlight: Set<String>` with `inFlight: [String: Task<PlatformImage?, Never>]`; on a hit, `await` the existing task's value instead of returning nil. Keeps the single-request-per-host property while giving every caller the result.
tests: FaviconServiceTests.testConcurrentFetchesForSameHostBothResolve — issue two overlapping fetchIcon(host:) calls against an injected stub and assert both return a non-nil image and only one network request was made

findings.claim: Typing a URL in the item editor fires a Google lookup per keystroke, sending partial/prefix hostnames to Google — including for items the user never saves.
findings.evidence:
Vaultify/Features/ItemEditor/ItemEditorScreen.swift:515 — `FaviconView(urlString: draft.urlField?.value, ...)` in the editor header. FaviconView.swift:47 `.task(id: faviconLoadKey)` with the key being the raw urlString (line 51), so every mutation of the text field re-runs load(). FaviconService.swift:21-27 accepts any non-empty string: "g" becomes "https://g" whose `URL.host` is "g", which then builds a valid request URL at line 42. There is no debounce, no minimum length, and no dot/TLD validation anywhere in FaviconService or FaviconView. The separate suggestion chip in WebsiteFieldRow.swift:65-70 does require a dot, but its own FaviconView (WebsiteFieldRow.swift:47) is a second, independent trigger.
Same class of leak in Vaultify/Features/ImportExport/ImportView.swift:67 — `ForEach(parsed.prefix(6)) { VaultItemRow(item: $0.item) }` renders favicons for parsed CSV rows in the import PREVIEW, before the user confirms the import.
findings.realRisk: Typing "github.com" sends google.com/s2/favicons requests for domain=g, gi, git, gith, githu, github, github.c, github.co, github.com. The prefix sequence is a stronger fingerprint than the final domain alone, and it is sent for drafts the user abandons. The import case is worse: hosts from a file the user is still deciding whether to import are already at Google. Also a pointless burst of network work on the app's most keyboard-heavy screen.
changeScope: Vaultify/Features/Components/FaviconView.swift:60-65 — add a short debounce (`try? await Task.sleep(...)` before the guard; `.task(id:)` cancels the prior task so the sleep swallows intermediate keystrokes) and require a plausible host before touching the network.

Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:21-27 — tighten `host(from:)` to reject hosts with no dot, a leading/trailing dot, or no TLD-shaped last label, so a partial typing state can never become a request.
Vaultify/Features/ImportExport/ImportView.swift:67 — pass an explicit opt-out (e.g. a `disablesFavicon` flag on VaultItemRow/FaviconView) so the pre-confirmation import preview never fetches.
tests: FaviconServiceTests.testHostRejectsPartialInput — host(from:) returns nil for "g", "git", "github", "github.", ".com"
FaviconViewTests / ItemEditor UI test — assert no fetch is issued for intermediate keystrokes of a typed URL
ImportViewTests.testPreviewDoesNotFetchFavicons — inject a counting FaviconService and assert zero requests while the import preview is on screen

findings.claim: Using URLSession.shared means Google's cookies persist in the shared cookie jar and the request URLs land in the default on-disk URLCache — neither is erased, so all favicon lookups from an install are correlatable to one pseudonymous identity.
findings.evidence: FaviconService.swift:46 — `try? await URLSession.shared.data(from: url)`. A repo-wide grep for URLSessionConfiguration, URLCache, `.ephemeral`, and httpCookie across Vaultify/ and VaultifyCore/ returns no configuration of any kind (only unrelated uses of the word "ephemeral" in the HPKE pairing code and UNAuthorizationStatus switches). URLSession.shared therefore uses HTTPCookieStorage.shared and the default disk-backed URLCache. AppEnvironment.swift:384-416 clears neither.
findings.realRisk: Google sets a NID cookie on the first s2/favicons request; every later favicon request from that install carries it, so the site list is not a stream of anonymous hits but one linked profile that persists across launches, across Erase Vault, and (for the cookie jar and cache, which live in Library/Cookies and Library/Caches) is reconstructible on-device. The cached HTTP responses also write the request URL — i.e. the domain — into a second plaintext location the erase path does not know about. This is the part that turns "Google can see the domains" into "Google can build a persistent per-device profile of this user's accounts", and it is invisible in the Settings disclosure text.
changeScope: Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:10-18,46 — hold a private `URLSession(configuration:)` built from `.ephemeral` (no persistent cookies, no disk cache) with `httpCookieStorage = nil`, `urlCache = nil`, `httpShouldSetCookies = false`, and a short `timeoutIntervalForRequest`; use it at line 46 instead of URLSession.shared. The service already owns its own disk cache, so the URLCache is pure downside.
tests: FaviconServiceTests.testSessionIsEphemeralAndCookieless — assert the service's session configuration has nil httpCookieStorage, nil urlCache, and httpShouldSetCookies == false
FaviconServiceTests.testRequestTimeoutIsBounded — assert timeoutIntervalForRequest is set (not the 60s default) so a captive portal cannot hang icon loads

findings.claim: Failed lookups are never remembered, so every offline or error-path host is re-requested on every single row appearance.
findings.evidence: FaviconService.swift:46-51 — on a non-200, a network error, or undecodable data the function returns nil at line 48 WITHOUT writing anything to `memory` or to disk. There is no negative-cache, no backoff, and no attempt counter anywhere in the 53-line file. FaviconView.swift:63-64 will call fetchIcon again on the next mount because the disk/memory lookup at FaviconService.swift:30-36 still misses.
findings.realRisk: On a flaky or offline connection every scroll of the vault list re-issues one request per visible row, forever. Beyond the battery and latency cost, it multiplies the exact thing the disclosure promises is a one-time-per-domain event — the header comment at FaviconService.swift:4-5 literally claims "each domain is fetched at most once", which is only true on the success path. Google therefore sees repeated, timestamped hits for the same host, which is a richer usage signal (when and how often the user opens their vault) than a single lookup.
changeScope: Vaultify/Services/FaviconService.swift:39-52 — record failures in a `failed: [String: Date]` map and skip re-fetch within a cooldown (and skip entirely when NetworkReachabilityMonitor reports unsatisfied — AppEnvironment.swift:186-190 already builds one); update the misleading header comment at FaviconService.swift:4-5.
tests: FaviconServiceTests.testFailedFetchIsNotRetriedImmediately — stub a failing transport, call fetchIcon twice, assert exactly one request
FaviconServiceTests.testFailureCooldownExpires — advance an injected clock past the cooldown and assert a retry is allowed

clusters.notes:
Blunt assessment of the audit's P0-04.

WHAT IT GOT RIGHT: the core claim is real and I confirmed every mechanical detail — default ON (SettingsStore.swift:237), Google s2/favicons with the raw host (FaviconService.swift:42), App Group cache keyed by plaintext domain (FaviconService.swift:16,32,50), no file protection on write (line 50, vs [.atomic, .completeFileProtection] everywhere else in this codebase), and the erase path genuinely never touches it (AppEnvironment.swift:384-416).

WHAT IT LIKELY OVERSTATED: if P0-04 said or implied "undisclosed", that is wrong. GeneralSettingsView.swift:86-88 and MacSettingsView.swift:133-135 carry an unusually honest footer that names Google by name and says exactly what leaks, and it is translated to vi and ja in Vaultify/Localizable.xcstrings. This is better disclosure than most commercial password managers ship. The defensible criticisms are (a) it is default-ON with no onboarding-time choice, and (b) README.md:3-6 and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy:22-60 contradict it — not that the user was never told.

WHAT IT GOT WRONG IF IT CLAIMED IT: the appex angle is refuted outright. Project.swift:221/287/336 scope the extensions to VaultifyAutoFill|VaultifySafari + VaultifyCore only; FaviconService/FaviconView are under Vaultify/ and cannot be linked there. Grepping the extension sources for URLSession/google.com finds nothing but a "pay.google.com" allowlist string. Do not let a report claim appex egress without this check — it inflates severity by an order of magnitude.

ALSO NOT A FETCH, DESPITE LOOKING LIKE ONE: ItemEditorScreen.swift:848 calls FaviconService.host(from:) purely to derive a title from a URL when the user left the title blank. Pure string parsing, zero network. If the audit counted it as a save-time lookup, that is wrong.

WHAT THE AUDIT MISSED (five items above): the duplicate-host rendering bug (NEW-1, the only user-visible defect here), per-keystroke and import-preview leakage (NEW-2), the URLSession.shared cookie/URLCache correlation problem (NEW-3, which is arguably the sharpest privacy edge in the whole cluster and is not covered by the Settings disclosure), and the never-cached failure path (NEW-4, which also makes the header comment at FaviconService.swift:4-5 factually false).

ON THE DEFAULT: I am deliberately NOT recommending you flip showWebsiteIcons to OFF unilaterally. Default-ON favicons is a legitimate product/UX decision and reversing it is a user-facing downgrade. The trade-off is: OFF preserves the "nothing leaves the device" claim verbatim but makes the vault list look plain out of the box; ON keeps the polish but requires you to (1) declare the disclosure in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy + the ASC App Privacy answers, (2) fix README.md's "only telemetry is GA4" line, and (3) ideally move the choice into onboarding. Pick one; the current state is the only combination that is not defensible.

ONE ADJACENT GAP OUTSIDE THIS CLUSTER, FOR THE RECORD: AppEnvironment.swift:384-416 also never touches attachmentStore. Vaultify/Services/AttachmentStore.swift has no erase API at all (only `directory` at line 47 and `url(for:)` at line 51), so `<AppGroup>/Attachments/*.enc` survives Erase Vault. Lower severity than the favicon cache — the filenames are opaque ids and the bytes are sealed under a key that session.resetVault() destroys — but it is the same omission pattern in the same function and belongs in whatever erase-path regression test you add.

I could not verify the App Store Connect privacy label answers (they live in ASC, not the repo) and there is no fastlane/metadata directory, so the marketing-copy risk is assessed from README.md only.

findings.claim: LockControlSnapshotTests fails because the slide-to-unlock arrow head disappears on Xcode/iOS 26.5 (SVG / symbol config / mask / stroke rendering regression).
findings.evidence: I ran the suite (Xcode 27.0, iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.3 sim, scheme Vaultify-Quality, -only-testing:VaultifySnapshotTests). All 3 snapshot tests fail. The recorded failure text is a SIZE mismatch, not a pixel diff: `Newly-taken snapshot@(390.0, 700.0) does not match reference@(260.0, 466.6666666666667)`. Reference PNG pixel dims: VaultifySnapshotTests/__Snapshots__/LockControlSnapshotTests/testSlideToUnlockLight.light-en.png = 780x240 (i.e. 390x120 @2x); both TutorialTooltip refs = 780x1400 (390x700 @2x). Read at displayScale 3 they resolve to 260x466.67pt, so SnapshotTesting bails before comparing pixels. I read the newly-taken render out of the sim container (.../tmp/LockControlSnapshotTests/testSlideToUnlockLight.light-en.png): the arrow renders COMPLETE — shaft plus head, white on the accent knob. Asset is fine: Vaultify/Assets.xcassets/PolarisIcons/ic_arrow_right.imageset/ic_arrow_right.svg (single evenodd path, `preserves-vector-representation: true`, `template-rendering-intent: template`), rendered via Vaultify/Features/Unlock/SlideToUnlock.swift:44 `VaultIcon(Icons.arrowRight, size: 20)` -> Vaultify/DesignSystem/Icons/Icons.swift:34 `ic_arrow_right`. Second, independent staleness: the committed reference shows a NEAR-BLACK knob ring; SlideToUnlock.swift:42 now strokes `Color(rgb: theme.accentForeground)` (white for the blue accent, VaultifyCore/Theme/AppTheme+Tokens.swift:74 `RGBMath.onAccent(...)`). `git log -S` proves the ring changed in 05444954 (2026-07-31, 'fix(unlock): slide knob ring in the on-accent color'), while the PNG was last written in 2f234b5e (2026-07-28). The reference was never re-recorded.
findings.realRisk: Nobody sees a broken arrow. The real damage is that all three snapshot references are device-scale-bound, so the suite can only ever pass on the exact @2x device that recorded them — and CI's pinned device (scripts/ci/create-simulator.sh: iPhone 17 Pro) is @3x. The suite is permanently red for its own harness reasons, which trains everyone to ignore it, and it masks the genuinely stale LockControl reference (a real, unreviewed visual change shipped on 2026-07-31).
changeScope: VaultifySnapshotTests/LockControlSnapshotTests.swift — pin the render scale so the reference is device-independent: pass `traits: UITraitCollection(displayScale: 3)` (or 2) to `.image(layout: .fixed(width:390,height:120), traits:)`.
VaultifySnapshotTests/TutorialTooltipSnapshotTests.swift — same `traits:` pin on both assertSnapshot calls.
VaultifySnapshotTests/__Snapshots__/LockControlSnapshotTests/testSlideToUnlockLight.light-en.png — re-record after the pin; the new render must show the white on-accent ring, not the near-black one.
VaultifySnapshotTests/__Snapshots__/TutorialTooltipSnapshotTests/*.png — re-record both at the pinned scale.
Vaultify/Assets.xcassets/PolarisIcons/ic_arrow_right.imageset/ — NO CHANGE. Do not touch the SVG; it renders correctly.
tests: LockControlSnapshotTests.testSlideToUnlockLight passes on BOTH an @2x and an @3x simulator after the traits pin (run the same test twice against two device types).

A guard test in VaultifyTests asserting every file under VaultifySnapshotTests/__Snapshots__ decodes at the pinned scale (e.g. pixelWidth == 390 * pinnedScale), so a re-record on the wrong device fails loudly instead of silently rebaselining.

findings.evidence: The test never reaches that line. findings.claim: VaultPanicRestartUITests.testDeliberateLockSurvivesRelaunch is blocked by the tutorial ('Add your first item'); the UI-test fixture needs an isolation mechanism for TutorialStore.
findings.evidence: Root cause proven for BOTH UI tests, not just this one. VaultPanicRestartUITests.swift:51 `XCTAssertTrue(element.isHittable)` fails. I extracted the last frame of the test's screen recording from the xcresult: it shows the tutorial card 'Step 2 of 3 — Check your security' over the Home screen with the Security tile spotlit — i.e. `settings.tap()` and the swipeUps were swallowed by the scrim, which ADVANCED the tour (Vaultify/DesignSystem/Tutorial/TutorialSpotlightOverlay.swift:89 `.onTapGesture { onNext() }`, hit shape at :85 has no hole because `awaitsRealTap` is false for firstRun step 1). Mechanism: Vaultify/App/AppEnvironment.swift:113-115 builds `settingsDefaults` from `UITestConfiguration.makeIsolatedSettingsDefaults()`, which at UITestConfiguration.swift:65 calls `removePersistentDomain` — so every UI-test launch gets a WIPED suite. AppEnvironment.swift:170 `self.tutorial = TutorialCoordinator(store: TutorialStore(defaults: settingsDefaults))`. TutorialStore.state(of:) returns `.notStarted` for a wiped suite and shouldPresent returns true (TutorialStore.swift:30-32, TutorialFeature.enabled == true at VaultifyCore/Tutorial/TutorialFeature.swift:11). HomeScreen.swift:239 `.task { env.tutorial.startIfNeeded(.firstRun) }` then fires after the 1200ms settleDelay (TutorialCoordinator.swift:21). The overlay covers pushed screens too: RootView.swift:48-49 applies `.tutorialHost(env.tutorial)` to `AdaptiveRootView()`, whose compact branch is `VaultUINavShell(env:)` — a UIViewControllerRepresentable — so the SwiftUI overlay sits ABOVE the whole UINavigationController including AppNavigator pushes (Settings, ItemDetail). HomeScreen.swift:243 `.onDisappear { cancelPendingStart() }` never fires for a UIKit push, so the timer is not cancelled either.
findings.realRisk: Both declared critical-journey UI tests are unrunnable, and so is the Maestro twin (quality/maestro/vault-edit-save-relock.yaml taps the same ids). The app's only end-to-end proof that edit→save→deliberate-lock→unlock preserves data, and that a deliberate lock survives a force-quit, does not execute. The panic-restart invariant is a security property (a shaken/locked vault must not relaunch into the frictionless path) with zero automated coverage today.
changeScope: Vaultify/App/AppEnvironment.swift — inside the existing `#if DEBUG if testIsolationEnabled { ... }` block (lines 128-142, same shape as `settings.onboardingCompleted = true`), hoist the tutorial store to a local and mark every flow answered: `let tutorialStore = TutorialStore(defaults: settingsDefaults)`; `if testIsolationEnabled { for id in TutorialFlow.allFlowIDs { tutorialStore.mark(id, .skipped) } }`; then line 170 becomes `self.tutorial = TutorialCoordinator(store: tutorialStore)`. No new launch argument, no new fixture case, no production behavior change.

tests: VaultifyUITests/VaultPanicRestartUITests.testDeliberateLockSurvivesRelaunch passes end to end.
VaultifyUITests/VaultEditSaveRelockUITests.testEditSaveLockAndUnlockPreservesItem passes end to end.
VaultifyTests: new assertion that under a UI-test fixture every TutorialFlow.allFlowIDs state is .skipped, so a future flow added to TutorialFlow.all cannot silently re-block the journey.

findings.claim: CI runs the quality suites and the release tag job depends on a green quality run for the same SHA.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml has exactly ONE job — `unit-tests` (:21) on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64, vaultify-ci]`, which runs `scripts/ci/run-xcode-suite.sh VaultifyTests ...` (:46-50) against a per-run simulator created by scripts/ci/create-simulator.sh (pinned iOS 26.5 runtime, iPhone 17 Pro) via scheme `Vaultify-Quality`. VaultifySnapshotTests and VaultifyUITests are NEVER run in CI. .github/workflows/release-ios.yml has exactly ONE job `release-ios` (:20) triggered by `push: tags: ['v*']` (:3-6) with NO `needs:`, no workflow_run gate, and no Actions-API query. Its only checks are: actor == triggering_actor == 'bervion' (:25), `git merge-base --is-ancestor $GITHUB_SHA origin/main` (:41), tag matches MARKETING_VERSION (:53-59), LOOX_LINK_PROD_TOKEN present (:66). `git show 200c961b -- .github/workflows/release-ios.yml` shows the deleted `release-preflight` job and the `needs: release-preflight` line that used to enforce it. The vestigial `permissions: actions: read` (:10) is the only trace left. IMPORTANT CONTEXT the audit must not steamroll: dropping the snapshot and critical-UI jobs was an EXPLICIT, documented owner decision in 1d64d656 (2026-07-26): 'ci: retire the snapshot and critical-UI jobs — Leftovers from an abandoned agent-team UI-testing experiment: the two jobs tripled every CI run on the self-hosted runner ... The test targets stay in the repo and remain runnable locally.' Re-adding them is a reversal of a user decision and needs the owner's call, not an audit fix.
findings.realRisk: `git tag v1.51.0 && git push --tags` uploads to TestFlight with zero test evidence — a red unit suite on main does not stop it, and a tag can point at a commit whose CI run was cancelled or never completed. Combined with the runbook (P0-05-05) still claiming a preflight gate exists, the release process is documented as gated and is in fact ungated.
changeScope: .github/workflows/release-ios.yml — add one step before 'Generate project with release configuration' that queries the CI workflow conclusion for $GITHUB_SHA (`gh api repos/${{github.repository}}/actions/runs?head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA` filtered to workflow ci.yml, require conclusion == success) and exits non-zero otherwise; this is what the existing but unused `permissions: actions: read` was for. docs/runbooks/ci-release-operations.md — either way, correct the 'Release procedure' section to state what is actually enforced.

.github/workflows/ci.yml — ONLY if the owner re-approves reversing 1d64d656: re-add snapshot-tests and critical-ui jobs (the deleted definitions are recoverable from `git show 200c961b:.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Do not do this unilaterally, and not before P0-05-01/03 make those suites green.

Fix: `nonisolated var hasWeakPassword` (the body is pure). (4) Vaultify/Security/Level2BiometricKeyStore.swift:137:9 'result of call to remove(group:) is unused' — the shared-group sweep discards its OSStatus while the private-group call is returned (:138). Correct fix is NOT a bare `_ =`: fold the statuses so a failed sweep is observable, e.g. `let shared = remove(group: SharedConfig.keychainAccessGroup); let own = remove(group: accessGroup); return own == errSecSuccess ? shared : own` (errSecItemNotFound must stay a success for both). (5)+(6) Vaultify/Services/AttachmentStore.swift:33:80 and :34:31 'main actor-isolated static property image / attachment ...' — `nonisolated struct AttachmentMeta` (:5) reads `Icons.image` / `Icons.attachment` from Vaultify/DesignSystem/Icons/Icons.swift:5, a MainActor-defaulted enum of `static let String`. Fix: `nonisolated enum Icons` (clears both, and (1) if IconResolver is done the same way). (7) Vaultify/Services/Tutorial/TutorialStore.swift:46:32 'main actor-isolated static property allFlowIDs ...' — `nonisolated final class TutorialStore` (:9) `resetAll()` reads `TutorialFlow.allFlowIDs` (Vaultify/Services/Tutorial/TutorialFlow.swift:29), which maps over `TutorialFlow.all` carrying LocalizedStringResource. Fix: take the ids as a parameter — `func reset(_ ids: [String])` called from the @MainActor TutorialCoordinator.replayAll() (TutorialCoordinator.swift:104) — rather than making TutorialFlow nonisolated. CORRECTION to the audit's framing: these are NOT Release-specific. Project.swift's only per-configuration settings are APS_ENVIRONMENT (:44-45); SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION=MainActor, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY and SWIFT_VERSION 5.0 are unconditional base settings (:38, :164-166), so all 7 appear in Debug too.

findings.claim: TutorialTooltipSnapshotTests.testClosingStepCardWithoutSkip does not just fail — it CRASHES the host app with SIGABRT.
findings.evidence: xcresult failure node for that test is `Crash: Vaultify at +[XCTFailableInvocation invokeErrorConventionInvocation:completion:]`. The crash report /Users/bervion/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Vaultify-2026-08-04-102804.ips decodes to EXC_CRASH / SIGABRT with faulting stack: `___BUG_IN_CLIENT_OF_LIBMALLOC_POINTER_BEING_FREED_WAS_NOT_ALLOCATED` <- malloc_report <- swift::TaskLocal::StopLookupScope::~StopLookupScope() <- swift_task_deinitOnExecutorImpl <- swift_task_deinitOnExecutorMainActorBackDeploy <- LooxEntitlementCoordinator.__deallocating_deinit <- _swift_release_dealloc <- AppEnvironment.init(uiTestConfiguration:) <- TutorialTooltipSnapshotTests.overlay(spotlight:shape:skip:). LooxEntitlementCoordinator is `@MainActor @Observable final class` with an `@ObservationIgnored private var inFlight: Task<Bool, Never>?` and no explicit deinit, so the compiler emits an isolated deallocating deinit routed through the back-deploy shim (deployment target is iOS 17.3, Project.swift:55). Trigger is constructing a second/third AppEnvironment in one process, which each snapshot test does.
findings.realRisk: Blocks the snapshot suite outright — even after P0-05-01 re-records the references, one of three tests aborts the process. Production exposure is low but not zero: AppEnvironment is created once per launch and normally never deallocated, but the same back-deployed isolated-deinit path ships to every user on iOS 17.3-18.x. Observed on Xcode 27.0 / iOS 26.3 sim; I could NOT check it on the pinned Xcode 26.5 because that version is not installed here (see NEW-2), so it may be a toolchain bug rather than app code.
changeScope: Reproduce first on the pinned toolchain before changing app code. findings.claim: scripts/ci/select-xcode.sh hard-pins Xcode 26.5, which exists nowhere on the maintainer machine — the release pipeline is one runner Xcode update away from being unable to ship.
findings.evidence: scripts/ci/select-xcode.sh:4 `EXPECTED_XCODE_VERSION="26.5"` and :5-9 probes only /Applications/Xcode_26.5.app, /Applications/Xcode_26.5.0.app, /Applications/Xcode.app; it exits 1 on any mismatch (:20-23). On this machine /Applications/Xcode.app is Xcode 26.6 and /Applications/Xcode-beta.app is 27.0. Running `bash scripts/ci/select-xcode.sh` prints 'Xcode 26.5 is required but was not found' and exits 1. That script is the SECOND step of both .github/workflows/ci.yml (:32-33) and .github/workflows/release-ios.yml (:36-37), and it is the first line of the runbook's compile-only release check (docs/runbooks/ci-release-operations.md:99). scripts/ci/create-simulator.sh:4 independently hard-pins `EXPECTED_IOS_RUNTIME_VERSION="26.5"`, and scripts/ci/prepare-project.sh:4 hard-pins Tuist 4.200.1.
findings.realRisk: An unattended Xcode update on the self-hosted vaultify-release runner turns every `v*` tag into a job that fails before it reaches signing — no build reaches TestFlight and the failure looks like an infrastructure outage, not a pin. The same pin means the maintainer cannot locally reproduce the CI/release toolchain at all, which is how P0-05-01 through P0-05-03 stayed undiagnosed. I could not verify the runner's actual installed Xcode from here.
changeScope: scripts/ci/select-xcode.sh — either bump EXPECTED_XCODE_VERSION to a version that is actually installed on the runner, or relax the match to a documented minimum (accept >= 26.5 and print the selected version) while keeping the hard failure when nothing qualifies.
scripts/ci/create-simulator.sh — same decision for EXPECTED_IOS_RUNTIME_VERSION so the runtime pin does not drift independently of the Xcode pin.
docs/runbooks/ci-release-operations.md — record the pin policy (exact vs minimum) and how to update it, next to the existing 'Runner is queued' troubleshooting entry.
tests: Run scripts/ci/select-xcode.sh on the release runner and on the maintainer machine; both must exit 0 and print the same major toolchain, or the doc must state the intended divergence.
Add a CI step that echoes the resolved DEVELOPER_DIR and xcodebuild -version into the unit-test receipt so a silent toolchain drift is visible in artifacts.

findings.claim: `make test` — the documented local quality command — is guaranteed red, because the auto-generated Vaultify scheme runs all three test targets.
findings.evidence: Makefile:104-107 `test: gen` runs `xcodebuild test -workspace Vaultify.xcworkspace -scheme $(SCHEME)` with `SCHEME := Vaultify` (:15). The Tuist-generated Vaultify.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/Vaultify.xcscheme TestAction lists three non-skipped TestableReferences: VaultifySnapshotTests, VaultifyTests and VaultifyUITests. So `make test` executes the suites proven broken in P0-05-01 (all 3 snapshot tests, one of them crashing) and P0-05-03 (both UI tests). Separately, Makefile:17 `DEST ?= platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16` contradicts CLAUDE.md's recorded finding that concrete named simulator destinations do not resolve in this environment, and Makefile:105 embeds the literal word `build` in the `check`/`lint` recipe, which the repo's own local hook blocks.
findings.realRisk: The one command a developer is told to run before pushing fails for reasons unrelated to their change, so it stops being run. That is the mechanism by which the ring-color regression (P0-05-01) and the tutorial blocker (P0-05-03) both shipped unnoticed. CI does not compensate: ci.yml only runs VaultifyTests.
changeScope: Makefile — point the `test` target at `-scheme Vaultify-Quality` (Project.swift:424-434 already declares it with the same three targets) and either scope it to VaultifyTests via `-only-testing:` for the fast path plus a separate `test-all`, or leave it broad but only after P0-05-01/NEW-1/P0-05-03 are fixed.
